case.pattern_description: A shared-device ring used one handset profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) behind an anonymising proxy to fraudulently access 28 different customers' cards in the same weeks, each time making purchases of $145.26-$145.26. This pattern affected multiple customers and matched 4 confirmed closed cases that could not be mapped to any known typology. The fraud was identified by tracing card -> transaction -> device in TigerGraph.

sar.narrative: Customer C06031, holder of card C06031-K2, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-11-25 13:57 and 2016-11-25 13:57, 1 transaction(s) totalling $145.26 were made on the card online from device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' through an anonymous proxy: $145.26 (3486052, 2016-11-25 13:57). The same device profile was used on 27 other customers' cards in the same period (C01289-K1, C01996-K2, C02910-K1, C02975-K1, C03676-K2, C04108-K2, C04274-K1, C05448-K2...), most of them behind anonymous proxies and each time as a new device, indicating a common actor. The activity is suspicious because: Device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' was used by 28 cards in a 60-day window around the alert; 28 of them behind an anonymous/hidden proxy and 28 flagged as a New device. 4 closed case(s) on cards that used this profile were confirmed fraud, 4 of them recorded as an undocumented pattern. It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-3008, CC-3902, CC-0562. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placed linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
